title: Quantization pilot & SLA playbook walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked MiraHealth through a hands-on Optimize pilot playbook for rolling out INT8/FP8 quantization profiles. Discussed SLA alignment, canary ramp plan, telemetry to watch (quality regressions, tail latency), and fallback rules. Customer raised questions about auditability, KMS, and worst-case rollback. Agreed next steps: run a 2-week sandbox with sample prompt set, share pilot checklist and pricing delta, schedule a 1-hour rollback/telemetry deep dive.
topics: Security: KMS, audit logs, data residency

Samir Patel: confirm VPC connectivity window for sandbox (due 2027-03-03)
next_steps: Start 2-week sandbox in Redwood Optimize with INT8 and FP8 profiles (target start 2027-03-07)

transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-28 10:00 AM PDT, Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Alex Torres (MiraHealth ML Eng), Priya Nair (MiraHealth CTO), Samir Patel (MiraHealth Infra)

[00:00] Jamie (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jamie from Redwood. Quick round robin — can each of you say where you're joining from and your role?
[00:12] Alex (Customer): Alex, ML eng in Boston, working on clinical summarization models.
[00:16] Priya (Customer): Priya, CTO, SF office — overseeing infra and compliance.
[00:20] Samir (Customer): Samir, infra, I manage clusters and networking.
[00:24] Jamie: Great. Ravi's our SE, he'll take most of the demo. Our goal today is to walk through a practical pilot for quantization profiles — INT8 and FP8 — and align on an SLA playbook for rolling it into production.
[00:35] Ravi (SE): Hey all. Quick agenda: 1) show Optimize console profiles and perf numbers, 2) discuss quality vs latency numbers on your sample prompts, 3) propose a canary ramp and rollback thresholds, 4) security/compliance notes.
[00:50] Alex: Sounds good. Our main question is: can we get the latency improvements without unacceptable degradation in clinical accuracy?
[00:57] Ravi: Totally. We'll show the kinds of metrics we collect and how to surface regressions. Note — some transcriptions call our product "Redwood Optima" in older docs but it's the same Optimize console.

[01:10] [Demo starts]
[01:12] Ravi: First slide — baseline with your current fp16-ish profile: median latency 180ms per request, p95 around 520ms at your current batch size. When we apply an INT8 profile we typically see median drop to ~110–120ms, p95 to ~300–350ms. FP8 lands in-between: median ~95–130ms depending on kernel and hardware. Caveat: numbers vary by sequence length and prompt shape.
[01:40] Priya: Wait, FP8 median is lower than INT8 in your slide? That seems counterintuitive.
[01:46] Ravi: Good catch. It's hardware and kernel dependent — on A100-family with our FP8 kernels FP8 can be slightly faster for the token path because it enables better TFMA kernel packing. On older gen cards INT8 might win. We'll map that for your target hardware.

[02:05] Alex: For clinical QA, we care about small hallucinations or paraphrase shifts. How do you quantify fidelity?
[02:12] Ravi: We recommend three levers: 1) automated semantic similarity + QA exact-match pass/fail on a labeled prompt set, 2) human spot checks on edgecases, 3) telemetry sampling in production for drift. In the console we compute delta-f1, BLEU-ish metrics, and a per-prompt fidelity flag.
[02:32] Samir: On telemetry, what retention and volume do you expose for the pilot? We can't ship PII to hosted logs.
[02:39] Jamie: Good point — for the sandbox you can run in our private/sandbox VPC or use our dedicated trial with customer-side log routing. We support KMS and can redact tokens. We'll share the pilot checklist describing exact artefacts we need, and the default telemetry retention is 30 days unless you request more.

[03:00] [Timestamped demo — console UI shown]
[03:05] Ravi: Here is the Optimize console. You create a quantization profile and select a safety margin (we call it a fidelity budget). You can pre-define fallback rules: if semantic-similarity drops below 0.88 for 5% of sampled prompts over a 1-hour window, roll back that profile.
[03:28] Priya: That threshold — 0.88 — is arbitrary for us. Can we set it per-route? We have a route used for patient-facing summaries that needs stricter tolerance.
[03:36] Ravi: Yes, profiles can be per-route and per-model. You can pin a stricter fidelity budget for that endpoint. The console also surfaces a heatmap of prompts that triggered quality flags.

[03:50] Alex: For the pilot we want both INT8 and FP8 runs. How does Redwood handle simultaneous variants?
[03:56] Ravi: You can spin up sandbox variants in parallel and use split routing — e.g., 5% INT8, 5% FP8, 90% baseline — for controlled A/B. The telemetry pipeline tags each response with profile metadata so you can compare side-by-side.

[04:18] [04:20] Jamie: Let's talk rollout playbook. We suggest a plan: 1) internal sandbox (5% traffic) for 3 days, 2) canary ramp to 20% for 4 days, 3) 50% for 3 days with intensive telemetry, 4) full roll. At each step we check three checks: quality metric delta, error/retry rate, and p95 tail latency changes.
[04:42] Samir: And an emergency rollback? The rollout needs to have automated fallback if error spike > 2x within 15 minutes, correct?
[04:49] Ravi: Exactly — we have automated fallback hooks. If error rate or semantic-failure rate exceeds configured thresholds, traffic is cut back to baseline for that route. You can also configure a slow-mode where requests are sent to a higher-fidelity model if latency is still within SLO.

[05:10] Priya: Are rollback actions auditable? We need an audit trail for compliance.
[05:14] Jamie: Yes, every automated or manual rollback is logged with a reason code, timestamp, and operator. We support pushing those logs to your SIEM or into a read-only S3 bucket encrypted with your KMS.

[05:28] [05:30] Alex: What about worst-case quality degradation — do you provide a simulation or stress test?
[05:35] Ravi: We can run a fidelity stress test in the sandbox: use your 500 prompts, amplify edge-cases, and run adversarial inputs to expose failure modes. We produce a per-prompt delta report and a suggested fallback map where certain prompt signatures always go to baseline.

[06:00] Alex: On hardware — if we go Dedicated, can we pin GPU types for INT8 vs FP8?
[06:06] Ravi: Yes, Dedicated pools can be configured by instance type. For FP8 we sometimes prefer newer architectures with FP8 kernel support. We'll include recommended hardware in the checklist. If you run private/on-prem, we provide kernel compatibility guidance but not the hardware.

[06:25] [06:30] Samir: Networking — we need a maintenance window to open VPC peering for the sandbox. I'll coordinate but prefer a mid-week small window.
[06:36] Jamie: Noted — action item for Samir to confirm window.

[06:40] [Quality examples segment]
[06:43] Ravi: Showing an example: prompt A (short clinical note) — INT8 produced identical summary in 98% of runs, FP8 99.1%. For long multi-paragraph notes, INT8 started showing compression artifacts around the 380 token mark; FP8 held slightly better. We recommend trying FP8 on long-document routes.
[07:10] Priya: Is there a cost delta? FP8 uses more permissive numeric formats — is it cheaper or more expensive generally?
[07:17] Jamie: Pricing depends on the kernel and runtime efficiency. Often FP8 gives similar or slightly better perf per token, but the accounting in our billing system treats them according to GPU cycles — we'll share a modeled pricing delta for your workload.

[07:35] Alex: About telemetry sampling — we don't want to upload PHI. Can we run local sampling and only send hashes and metrics?
[07:42] Ravi: Yes — you can enable client-side redaction. The sandbox can be configured to never leave the private VPC or to push only pseudonymized telemetry. We documented common redaction patterns in the pilot checklist.

[08:00] [08:02] Priya: How long does the pilot contract look like? We prefer a short bounded engagement.
[08:06] Jamie: Standard is 2–4 weeks for sandbox. We usually do a 2-week technical pilot, then extend if you need more time for edgecases. We'll send a one-page pilot agreement.

[08:20] [Detailed rollback examples]
[08:25] Ravi: Example rule: if p95 latency improvement is < 10% but semantic delta > 5% across sampled prompts for 2 hours, abort ramp and rollback. Another: if error rate increases 2x or more for system errors (5xx), immediate rollback. These thresholds are tunable.

[08:50] Alex: If we see a small systematic bias in outputs after INT8, can we run a short calibration pass (recalibration of qprofiles)?
[08:58] Ravi: Yes — Optimize includes a qprofile sweep tool that runs micro-batches of calibration data to re-tune the scale factors; it's an automated pass you can trigger as part of the pilot. We recommend keeping a versioned snapshot of each qprofile for traceability.

[09:20] Samir: Security: SSO, SAML, RBAC? We need role separation for who can change profiles vs who can view telemetry.
[09:27] Jamie: Support for SSO, SAML, SCIM, and fine-grained RBAC is available on Dedicated/Private and for Hosted Enterprise tiers. For pilots we can simulate RBAC with scoped API keys.

[09:40] [Wrap-up and concerns]
[09:42] Priya: My main concern is the human review bandwidth — we'll need a clear list of high-risk prompts to prioritize.
[09:47] Ravi: We'll produce a prioritized risk list from the initial sweep; it ranks by delta severity and projected user-facing impact.

[09:58] Jamie: Recap of next steps: Ravi will share the pilot checklist and telemetry queries; Jamie will send pricing and pilot contract; Alex will supply the 500 prompt set; Samir will confirm VPC window. We'll meet after 1 week of the sandbox for the telemetry deep dive.
[10:16] Priya: Ok, sounds good.
[10:18] Alex: One more — can we get a simple runbook we can hand to on-call?
[10:22] Jamie: Yes — we'll include a 1-page on-call runbook with thresholds and the automated rollback commands.
[10:26] Samir: Thanks, everyone.
[10:30] Jamie: Thanks — we'll follow up with the checklist and docs.

[END]

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present ("K-V cash" noted once in console notes, and an earlier slide label read "Redwood Optima"). Links referenced: pilot checklist (internal): https://redwood.ai/pilot-checklist.pdf , sample deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/quant-sla-playbook.pdf
